{{Short description|Mathematical concept}}
In mathematics, specifically in [[order theory]] and [[functional analysis]], two elements ''x'' and ''y'' of a [[vector lattice]] ''X'' are '''lattice disjoint''' or simply '''disjoint''' if <math>\inf \left\{ |x|, |y| \right\} = 0</math>, in which case we write <math>x \perp y</math>, where the '''absolute value''' of ''x'' is defined to be <math>|x| := \sup \left\{ x, - x \right\}</math>.{{sfn | Schaefer | Wolff | 1999 | pp=204–214}} 
We say that two sets ''A'' and ''B'' are '''lattice disjoint''' or '''disjoint''' if ''a'' and ''b'' are disjoint for all ''a'' in ''A'' and all ''b'' in ''B'', in which case we write <math>A \perp B</math>.{{sfn | Schaefer | Wolff | 1999 | pp=74–78}} 
If ''A'' is the singleton set <math>\{ a \}</math> then we will write <math>a \perp B</math> in place of <math>\{ a \} \perp B</math>. 
For any set ''A'', we define the '''disjoint complement''' to be the set <math>A^{\perp} := \left\{ x \in X : x \perp A \right\}</math>.{{sfn | Schaefer | Wolff | 1999 | pp=74–78}}

== Characterizations ==

Two elements ''x'' and ''y'' are disjoint if and only if <math>\sup\{ | x |, | y | \} = | x | + | y |</math>. 
If ''x'' and ''y'' are disjoint then <math>| x + y | = | x | + | y |</math> and <math>\left(x + y \right)^{+} = x^{+} + y^{+}</math>, where for any element ''z'', <math>z^{+} := \sup \left\{ z, 0 \right\}</math> and <math>z^{-} := \sup \left\{ -z, 0 \right\}</math>.

== Properties ==

Disjoint complements are always [[Band (order theory)|bands]], but the converse is not true in general. 
If ''A'' is a subset of ''X'' such that <math>x = \sup A</math> exists, and if ''B'' is a subset lattice in ''X'' that is disjoint from ''A'', then ''B'' is a lattice disjoint from <math>\{ x \}</math>.{{sfn | Schaefer | Wolff | 1999 | pp=74–78}}

=== Representation as a disjoint sum of positive elements ===

For any ''x'' in ''X'', let <math>x^{+} := \sup \left\{ x, 0 \right\}</math> and <math>x^{-} := \sup \left\{ -x, 0 \right\}</math>, where note that both of these elements are <math>\geq 0</math> and <math>x = x^{+} - x^{-}</math> with <math>| x | = x^{+} + x^{-}</math>.  
Then <math>x^{+}</math> and <math>x^{-}</math> are disjoint, and <math>x = x^{+} - x^{-}</math> is the unique representation of ''x'' as the difference of disjoint elements that are <math>\geq 0</math>.{{sfn | Schaefer | Wolff | 1999 | pp=74–78}} 
For all ''x'' and ''y'' in ''X'', <math>\left| x^{+} - y^{+} \right| \leq | x - y |</math> and <math>x + y = \sup\{ x, y \} + \inf\{ x, y \}</math>.{{sfn | Schaefer | Wolff | 1999 | pp=74-78}} 
If ''y ≥ 0'' and ''x'' ≤ ''y'' then ''x''<sup>+</sup> ≤ ''y''. 
Moreover, <math>x \leq y</math> if and only if <math>x^{+} \leq y^{+}</math> and <math>x^{-} \leq x^{-1}</math>.{{sfn | Schaefer | Wolff | 1999 | pp=74–78}}
